map.由面纸、里纸、芯纸环压强度与瓦楞类型估算纸板边压强度 ECT，再用 McKee: Estimate the board edge crush strength ECT from the liner, middle, and flute strengths and the flute type, then compute empty box compression strength BCT with the McKee formula, returning the safe stacking layers and height.
map.运输包装设计中，由瓦楞纸板边压(ECT)估算箱体抗压(BCT)，定堆码层数。: In transport packaging design, estimate box compression (BCT) from board edge crush (ECT) to set the stacking layers.
map.纸箱选型时，按货物重量与安全系数反推所需 ECT 与楞型。: When selecting a box, work backward from the cargo weight and safety factor to the required ECT and flute type.
map.仓储规划中，由 BCT 与安全系数核算单层承重与最大堆高。: In warehouse planning, use BCT and the safety factor to work out the per-layer load capacity and the maximum stacking height.
map.算例：A 楞箱抗压（ECT 估算，400×300×300mm，箱重 15kg）: Worked example: compression of a C-flute box (ECT estimate, 400×300×300 mm, box weight 15 kg)
map.：ECT≈(4000+4000+2500×1.53)×0.5≈5913 N/m；: : ECT ≈ (4000+4000+2500×1.53)×0.5 ≈ 5913 N/m; BCT = 5.87×ECT×√(perimeter×thickness) = 5.87×5913×√(1.4×0.0036) ≈ 2464 N (about 251 kgf); with a safety factor of 3 the safe load is about 821 N, allowing roughly 6 layers and a stack height of about 1.8 m. Formula: BCT = 5.87·ECT·√(Pm·d).
map.：单层货重=15×9.81≈147 N；最大堆层数=floor(安全载荷/单层货: : weight per layer = 15×9.81 ≈ 147 N; maximum layers = floor(safe load / weight per layer) + 1 = floor(821/147) + 1 = 6 layers. Stack height = 6×0.3 = 1.8 m. A smaller safety factor allows fewer layers.

map.这是 McKee 经验公式的常用形式，适用于规则开槽箱(RSC)、瓦楞方向正确的: This is the common form of the McKee empirical formula, valid for regular slotted containers (RSC) with the ECT entered in the correct flute direction. ECT can be estimated from the liner and middle sheet strengths and the flute take-up factor (ECT ≈ (liner + liner + middle × takeup) × efficiency), or measured and entered directly.
map.一般运输仓储取 3–5，潮湿/长周期/自动堆码取高值。它综合温湿度、堆码时间、振: Ordinary transport and warehousing uses 3–5, while damp, long-cycle, or fully automated stacking calls for the higher end. It combines temperature and humidity, stacking time, vibration, and handling factors; too small a safety factor risks collapse and too large wastes material and raises cost.
